skill.name: uniprot-database
skill.description: Search UniProt, retrieve protein sequences and annotations, map identifiers, and stream large result sets through the REST API or bundled Python client.
skill.summary: Query UniProt for protein records, sequences, annotations, and identifier mappings.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate UniProt client and reference package with no prompt injection, secret collection, command execution, or suspicious destinations. Most static findings are Markdown, JavaScript template literals, official UniProt requests, or harmless terminology. Two download examples can overwrite files, and the client lacks bounded network waits.

remediation.issue: Download examples can overwrite existing files.
remediation.suggestion: Refuse existing destinations by default and require an explicit overwrite option after user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Network calls and ID mapping polling can wait indefinitely.
remediation.suggestion: Set connection and read timeouts, cap polling duration, handle failed jobs, and return a clear timeout error.

content.value_statement: Protein research often requires precise searches, sequences, annotations, and identifier mappings from UniProt. This skill provides direct REST workflows and a Python client for repeatable protein data access.
actual_capabilities: Search UniProtKB with Boolean, field-specific, range, taxonomy, and review-status filters.
Retrieve individual protein records in JSON, TSV, XML, FASTA, RDF, text, and related formats.
Map identifiers between UniProt and supported databases through asynchronous ID mapping jobs.
Batch retrievals and stream large result sets to reduce pagination overhead.
List available result fields and supported ID mapping databases with the bundled Python client.
limitations: Requires internet access and depends on UniProt API availability and response formats.
Bundled requests omit explicit network timeouts, retries, caching, and a maximum polling duration.
ID mapping accepts at most 100,000 identifiers per job, and UniProt stores results for seven days.
Download examples can overwrite existing local files unless the caller checks the destination first.

use_cases.title: Find curated protein records
use_cases.description: Find reviewed proteins by gene, function, organism, taxonomy, or annotation and retrieve focused fields for analysis.

use_cases.title: Build bioinformatics workflows
use_cases.description: Integrate sequence retrieval, batch search, streaming, and identifier mapping into Python workflows or command-line pipelines.

use_cases.title: Normalize biological identifiers
use_cases.description: Convert accession sets across UniProt, Ensembl, RefSeq, PDB, GO, and other supported identifier systems.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve a protein sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the reviewed UniProt entry for human insulin. Return the primary accession, protein name, sequence length, and FASTA sequence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for one known protein

prompt_templates.title: Build a focused protein search
prompt_templates.prompt: Search reviewed human BRCA1 proteins. Return accession, gene names, protein name, length, function, disease comments, and PDB cross-references in a concise table.

prompt_templates.title: Map identifiers across databases
prompt_templates.prompt: Map these RefSeq protein identifiers to UniProtKB and Ensembl: {identifiers}. Report successful mappings, failed identifiers, and one-to-many relationships.

prompt_templates.title: Design a scalable retrieval workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a rate-limited workflow for this UniProt query: {query}. Select required fields, handle pagination or streaming, add timeouts, and prevent accidental file overwrites.

output_examples.input: Find the reviewed human insulin entry and summarize it.
output: A FASTA sequence and selected annotations are included.

output_examples.input: Map P01308 and P04637 from UniProtKB to PDB.
output: A UniProt identifier mapping job was submitted.
Matched PDB identifiers are grouped by source accession.
Failed and one-to-many mappings are reported separately.

output_examples.input: Prepare a reviewed human kinase FASTA download.
output_examples.output: A reviewed human kinase query is prepared. Results are streamed in chunks to the selected destination with overwrite checks.

best_practices: Prefer reviewed:true when curated Swiss-Prot records are required.
Request only needed fields and choose FASTA, TSV, or JSON according to downstream use.
Set timeouts, rate limits, polling deadlines, and overwrite checks before running large downloads.
anti_patterns: Do not treat unreviewed TrEMBL predictions as manually curated evidence.
Do not stream broad datasets without estimating result size and choosing a destination.
Do not pass unvalidated file paths or overwrite existing results without explicit approval.

faq.question: Does this skill require a UniProt API key?
faq.answer: No. The included workflows use public UniProt REST endpoints without authentication.

faq.question: Can it search reviewed and unreviewed entries?
faq.answer: Yes. Use reviewed:true for Swiss-Prot or reviewed:false for TrEMBL entries.

faq.question: Which output formats are supported?
faq.answer: The references cover JSON, TSV, Excel, XML, FASTA, RDF, text, GFF, and related endpoint-specific formats.

faq.question: Can it map identifiers from other databases?
faq.answer: Yes. The ID mapping workflow supports UniProt, Ensembl, RefSeq, PDB, GO, and many other listed databases.

faq.question: Can it handle large result sets?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports pagination, batching, and streaming, but callers should add timeouts, rate limits, and bounded polling.

faq.question: Does it write files automatically?
faq.answer: The bundled client prints results. Some reference download examples write files and can overwrite existing destinations.
